title: Community Roles
description: How the member, moderator, and admin tier model shapes participation and shared responsibility.
content:
# Community Roles

Karmyq communities use a three-tier role model designed around a simple principle: **people who show up consistently should have the tools to help run things**, without necessarily owning the community's structure and configuration.

## The Three Tiers

### Member

The default role for anyone who joins a community. Members can:
- View the community Overview and Norms
- Browse the member directory (card view)
- Post and respond to help requests through the main feed

Members do not see admin-facing tabs (Requests, Insights, Settings, Providers).

### Moderator

Moderators are trusted, active members who help run the community's day-to-day operations. They are typically people who are densely connected within the network — people who know the community well and are known by it.

Moderators can:
- Approve or reject pending member applications
- Invite new members
- View the Active/Pending member filter and member table
- Access the Requests tab — view open help requests, override urgency, add internal notes, and propose a connector match
- View community statistics and network cohesion in the Insights tab
- Access the Providers tab

Moderators cannot:
- Change member roles (promote/demote)
- Remove members
- Access the Settings tab (community configuration, TTL/decay, linked communities)
- Export community data

The moderator role is granted by an admin through the Members tab role dropdown.

### Admin

Admins have full control. In addition to everything a moderator can do, admins can:
- Change member roles (including promoting to moderator)
- Remove members
- Access the Settings tab — configure community description, norms TTL, karma decay, and linked communities
- Export community data from the Insights tab
- Access all provider settings

The community founder is automatically the first admin.

## Why This Model

The division between moderator and admin follows an **operations vs. governance** boundary.

Moderators own operations: they keep the community moving — approving members, triaging requests, connecting people. Admins own governance: they control who gets what role, how the community is configured, and what data can be exported.

This means a community can distribute the day-to-day work of running things across several trusted people without giving everyone the ability to reconfigure the community or export sensitive data.

## Triage and Match Proposal

One of the most important moderator capabilities is the **Requests tab triage workflow**:

1. Open the Requests tab (visible to moderators and admins)
2. Click **Triage** on any open request
3. Override the urgency level if needed (low / medium / high / critical)
4. Add an internal admin note — visible only to admins and moderators, not to members
5. Optionally propose a connector: select an active community member to match with the requester

When a match is proposed, the requester is notified and must accept before the match is confirmed.

## Migration Note

The moderator role has existed in the database since the community system launched. Communities that already have moderators will see their moderators gain these new capabilities automatically — no re-configuration needed.
